title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 Flow Control Verification Work Item
summary: Document how RFC 9250 flow control maps to the shared QUIC transport runtime and add focused contract tests that prove the transport enforces aggregate connection limits, per-stream limits, stream-creation limits, handshake transport parameters, and 0-RTT remembered limits.
planned_changes:
- Update the RFC 9250 SPEC trace links for REQ-0116 through REQ-0123.
- Add ARC-QUIC-RFC9250-0021 to document the transport mapping.
- Add verification-oriented contract tests under `tests/Incursa.Quic.Tests/RequirementHomes/RFC9250/REQ-QUIC-RFC9250-0021.cs`.
- Prove aggregate connection receive limits, per-stream receive limits, stream-creation limits, transport-parameter round-tripping, runtime handshake commit enforcement, and 0-RTT remembered-limit behavior through the shared QUIC runtime.
- Do not add a custom DoQ flow-control layer.
- Do not add DoQ-specific defaults unless a transport gap is discovered during verification.
verification_plan: Run the focused flow-control requirement-home tests, core SpecTrace JSON validation, and diff hygiene checks after the SPEC trace links are updated.
out_of_scope: Changing shared QUIC transport semantics for other protocols.
completion_notes: The transport layer already owns the flow-control behavior. This slice only adds trace alignment and proof coverage, including the runtime commit path that applies peer transport parameters into bookkeeping limits.
